title: Turn a Plastic Basket Into a Stunning Concrete Planter! 🧺✨
description:
Looking for a unique way to upgrade your garden or front porch decor without breaking the bank? In this video, we turn an ordinary plastic mesh basket into a high-end, textured concrete planter!
This step-by-step DIY tutorial shows you how to mix, mold, and paint a gorgeous cement flower pot featuring a modern grid design and a custom scalloped edge. It’s an incredibly affordable, beginner-friendly weekend project that looks like it came straight from an upscale home decor boutique.

Materials & Steps Shown:
 Materials Used: Plastic mesh basket, packing tape, concrete mix, sand, inner cylinder core, PVC pipe (for drainage), outdoor yellow paint.
 Step 1: Wrap the outer mesh basket securely in packing tape to seal the mold.
 Step 2: Pour a concrete base and use a trowel to shape a decorative scalloped edge.
 Step 3: Place the basket mold down, insert a center core filled with sand, and pour the concrete walls.
 Step 4: Push a small PVC pipe into the center to create a built-in drainage hole.
 Step 5: Let it cure, demold, clear out the sand, and finish with a vibrant coat of paint!

title: Underwater Wine Opening Method 🥂
description:
Original video credit: IG/@duefriulaniingiro.

This method is used for natural sparkling wines that haven’t been disgorged. In standard champagne production, the neck of the bottle is frozen so the dead yeast from fermentation can be removed before sale. Some winemakers skip this step, leaving the sediment inside to preserve the wine and develop more complex flavors over time.

Because of that sediment, opening the bottle normally would mix everything together and likely cause a messy, high-pressure overflow. To avoid this, the bottle is stored upside down for at least a day so the yeast collects near the cork.

When opening, the neck of the bottle is submerged upside down in cold water. As the cork is released, the pressure forces the compacted sediment out into the water. The water catches the discharge and prevents the wine from spraying.

After a couple of seconds, the flow clears and the bottle is turned upright. The result is a clean, clear pour, while the sediment stays behind in the water. It’s a practical solution that also makes for a striking presentation.
